A is moderately more expensive. And furthermore, when there's the circumstances where the tar depth is big is, of course, meaningful on the spectrum. However, when it is especially premium is when it ends up being a differentiator where other properties are also high on the spectrum. So, for example, if, for example, shade is equal at the top, let's say it's pale, and that's tied. And then let's also assume that vintage is also high at 20, let's say high, when tar is the absolute highest relative to something that's just a shade or adjacent under, then it makes a big difference, because to be high on the spectrum in all four attributes is especially difficult and rare. So when faced with A or B, and all four, suppose, are being compared, all four attributes are being compared, and three out of the four for each are high, and then one happens to have all four, then it becomes especially meaningful, because it's so difficult to have that advantage in one attribute, let alone four. And to have it suggests not only a premium unto itself, but relative to the other attributes and to the competition's attributes.
